clue.text: Old Central Vietnam returns this food

indicators.note: returns tells us the old region's name is read backwards here

parts.note: Annam was the old name for the central region of Vietnam

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a traditional dish coming back to the menu in central Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ANNAM round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the miraculous food given to the Israelites in the wilderness.

clue.text: As dominant as' one leaving the high table ?

definitions.text: As dominant as' one leaving the high table

parts.words: As dominant as' one leaving the high table
parts.note: a college master who has dined at the high table leaves it full, and those two words together mean domineering

explanation.walkthrough: Split as MASTER FUL(L): the head of an Oxbridge college, well fed after dinner at the high table, the top table in a college hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanding and domineering, imposing one's will.

clue.text: "Hardy as the Nemean lion's -" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Hamlet, defying his friends to follow the ghost, says each artery is as hardy as the sinew of the Nemean lion

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hamlet Act 1 Scene 4: 'And makes each petty artery in this body / As hardy as the Nemean lion's nerve.'
explanation.definitionFit: Here the word means a sinew or tendon, the old sense used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: They measure 'the current of a stream swirling round me

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the next word
swirling suggests the stream's letters churning into a new order

explanation.surface: Instruments gauge the flow of water eddying about the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes AMTERS from STREAM, and 'round' places it about ME. 'current' suggests water, but it is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument for measuring electric current in amperes.

clue.text: Sheffield product has inner core altered to make coffee

indicators.note: has inner means the plate holds something in its middle

parts.note: Sheffield is famous for its silver plate and cutlery

indicators.note: altered shows the letters of core are rearranged before going in

explanation.surface: A Sheffield factory changes the core of its product to start brewing coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' makes ERCO from CORE, and 'has inner' puts it inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to brew coffee by passing boiling water repeatedly through the grounds.

clue.text: Stern — backward, too

indicators.note: backward, too says the word reads the same when written in reverse

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A severe person is also behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome; 'Stern' is the rear of a ship, not severe.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the raised deck at the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Given extra strength by breaking a fine record

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of the phrase being smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An athlete is fortified by setting a good new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges FINE RECORD; 'breaking a record' is the misleading surface phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforced means strengthened with additional support or material.

clue.text: Equipment shows, success of hospitalization

explanation.surface: A patient's kit is a sign of a successful hospital stay.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of gear or clothing; and leaving hospital fully recovered is being out and fit.

clue.text: With this device one can change the inside of fruit

indicators.note: the inside of means the new letters go into the middle of the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: change means the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget lets you alter the core of an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' makes IANC from I CAN, and 'the inside of' puts it into APPLE between L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine designed for a particular task.

clue.text: Like being included in retreating general's stand

indicators.note: being included in means one piece is placed inside the other
retreating means the general's name is read backwards

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
as means like

explanation.surface: A retreating general makes a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns LEE into EEL, and 'being included in' puts AS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame for supporting a painting.

clue.text: Fiery-headed one may storm and boil wildly

indicators.note: wildly signals that storm and boil are thrown into disorder to form a new word

explanation.surface: A hot-headed person may rage and seethe out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges the letters of STORM and BOIL together. 'Fiery-headed one' sounds like a hothead but is a volcano with fire at its summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is an Italian island volcano, constantly erupting from its crater top.

clue.text: A quiet setback about the records

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: read as two words, set back: the word set written backwards
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet disappointment surrounds the archive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a single noun but splits as 'set back', giving TES; 'about' wraps it round A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapes are recordings, made on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Puts up with reformation in Southern Crete

indicators.note: reformation suggests the island's name being formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Southern Crete tolerates a religious reform movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformation' turns CRETE into ERECT, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building is to construct or raise it.

clue.text: Though authorized, it's. not on here in Paris, Mr Capone

parts.note: off is the opposite of on, as a switch
ici is French for here
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A Chicago gangster abroad is told a deal is off, despite approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Something official has been sanctioned by those in authority.

clue.text: Permissive deviations make the Spanish 'cry in ecstasies

indicators.note: in means the cry is set inside the other word

parts.note: trances are states of rapture
ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Lenient attitudes lead the Spanish to cry out in rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish' looks like EL, but 'the Spanish cry' together gives OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerances are the allowable variations from a standard measurement.

clue.text: A plank to walk? This should stump the examiners

parts.note: to floor someone is to stump or baffle them
a board is a panel of examiners

explanation.surface: A trick question about walking the plank to baffle the examining panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A plank to walk' recalls pirates, but means a plank of wood underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Floorboards are the wooden planks laid to form a floor you walk on.

clue.text: Ticket from Athens 'to Coventry

parts.note: in ancient Athens a citizen was banished by votes scratched on potsherds; sending someone to Coventry is the British idiom for refusing to speak to them

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a rail fare; Athenians voted to banish someone by writing the name on a pottery shard (ostrakon). 'Sent to Coventry' is British for being shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion from society or a group by general consent.

clue.text: The only time to begin a fairy tale

explanation.surface: A storyteller is allowed a single chance to start a fairy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Done only on one occasion; and 'Once upon a time' is the traditional opening of fairy stories.

clue.text: Assesses quotations

explanation.surface: A valuer reviews the quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge approximately; builders' estimates are price quotations.

clue.text: Little man with wild dog but no love for reputation

parts.note: Stan is a short form of the man's name Stanley

indicators.note: but no love means the letter for zero, love in tennis, is removed

parts.note: the dingo is the Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A small man with a feral dog but no affection worries about his standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the shortened name STAN; love is O in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's status or repute.

clue.text: Spoil sound of this instrument

indicators.note: sound of means the word for spoil is said out loud to give the answer

parts.note: loot means spoils or plunder

explanation.surface: A musician complains that bad sound has ruined their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' looks like a verb but is the noun, plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body.

clue.text: Felt by men posted again to the front?

definitions.text: Felt by men posted again to the front?

parts.words: Felt by men posted again to the front
parts.note: soldiers sent a second time to the battle line would feel bitter, and being sent again plus men spells out the word

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as RE-SENT MEN T: the feeling of soldiers sent back to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness at unfair treatment is the emotion described.

clue.text: Precipitate way of making a living

explanation.surface: A hasty choice of profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong; a career is one's profession.

clue.text: Impetuous youth has to dash off.

parts.note: to tear is to dash or rush
away means off, gone

explanation.surface: A reckless young person rushes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, reckless young person.

clue.text: Is. the Head in. charge of this subject?

parts.note: top means head, the uppermost part
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A pupil asks whether the headteacher is responsible for this lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Head' suggests a headteacher but just gives TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion.

clue.text: Where the worker has the edge

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's classic worker
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A question about the place where an employee holds an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' is the definition: Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland, so a place.

clue.text: Plants needing more air for sound growth

definitions.text: Plants needing more air for sound growth

parts.words: Plants needing more air for sound growth
parts.note: marsh plants whose stems make the vibrating tongues of wind instruments, which need breath blown through them to sound

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound growth' looks like healthy growth, but the plants give the vibrating strips in woodwind, which need air to make a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall water-side grasses whose stems also supply instrument mouthpieces.

annotationWithheld.clue: Responsibility is burdensome without 'a Cockney hero'

clue.text: Mysterious author holds one point in balance

indicators.note: holds means the author's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote mystery and horror tales
I is the Roman numeral one
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A writer of mysteries keeps a point balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts I and S inside POE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is a steady equilibrium of body or mind.

clue.text: Temperate 'over the Channel

explanation.surface: A note that the weather is mild across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent can mean self-restrained or moderate; and to the British the Continent is mainland Europe across the English Channel.

clue.text: Includes' care of Military. Police pay increases

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
MP is the abbreviation for Military Police
rises is the British word for pay raises

explanation.surface: An army police payslip lists raises among its items.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rise' is British for a pay raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to consist of or contain.

clue.text: Blows Old Possum's Theatre Cat out of the way

parts.note: Gus the Theatre Cat is a poem in Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
Old Possum was T. S. Eliot's nickname, so his initials are TS

explanation.surface: Eliot's elderly theatrical cat is moved aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost its opening words; the scan restores them. T. S. Eliot wrote Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, whose Gus the Theatre Cat is followed by the poet's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusts are sudden strong rushes of wind.
